svg.aria-label: AnomaEYE architecture overview: cameras at a site publish video to a cloud media server; a GPU service scores every stream and a vision-language verifier confirms candidates; the backend stores the event and evidence and alerts staff by app, SMS, email and an on-site siren.
svg.text: From a camera on site to a verified alert on a guard's phone. The numbers 1 to 6 follow one detection.
dashed: the arrow's tail makes the request (pull or poll)
existing CCTV, RTSP on the LAN
video to the cloud, no re-encoding
ESP32 siren plus a small agent that
serves live view to the apps
nothing is archived without an event
one organisation per tenant, role-based access
stores the event, cuts the evidence clip
sends alerts, pushes live updates to the apps
records every action in an audit trail
live video to viewers (WebRTC, HLS fallback)
JSON API and live updates over WebSocket
siren command, collected by the site agent
push and SMS on the same phone
Operators see the cameras assigned to them; admins manage their
own organisation; nobody sees another organisation's cameras or events.
A siren at the site sounds for severe events (step 6, lower left).
GPU pulls each registered camera's video

1 camera agent sends video · 2 GPU pulls the stream · 3 gate proposes, verifier confirms · 4 verified detection delivered · 5 event stored, clip cut from the buffer, alerts sent · 6 staff alerted on phone and dashboard; siren sounds on site
Releases: git push, Cloud Build, then a blue-green swap of the API on the VM; the media server is never restarted, so a release never drops a live stream.
Privacy: no face recognition; video is kept only around a confirmed event; evidence is private and shared by short-lived links; every verdict and human action is logged.
